reflections.title: "Do Not Fear, for I Am with You"

reflect.text: When we face overwhelming seasons, deep tiredness, or anxious thoughts, our own inner strength quickly runs dry. We easily look at our problems like stormy winds and rough waves, fearing that our feet will slip. Yet God does not scold us for feeling helpless or troubled. Instead, He draws near with tender mercy, assuring us that we are never left to wander through hard times alone.

The Lord promises to give us inward strength and to stand beside us as our helper. The same God who created the universe, steers the earth, and keeps the stars burning has limitless power for our daily needs. He gives us quiet calm during sudden trials, supplying the exact help we need right where we are most frail.

Because God is completely righteous and true to His word, this promise is an anchor we can lean on for life. He stretches out His strong right hand to keep us from falling. When we step forward in faith upon His word, we find solid rock beneath our feet, held fast by a God who will never let us down.

questions: In what area of your life do you feel your own strength running dry right now?
How does knowing God is holding you with His righteous right hand ease your worries?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for drawing near to me when I feel tired, anxious, and weak. Please fill me with Your strength today, and uphold me with Your mighty right hand. Help me fix my eyes on You and rest peacefully in Your faithful care. Amen.

D11.author: Jennifer Slattery
D11.work: How God Deals With Our Anxiety

reflections.title: God’s Faithful Help for His People

reflect.text: Just as trees need daily rain and our bodies need food, our souls need regular renewal from God. We cannot keep going on our own reserves. When we neglect prayer and God's Word, our spiritual life grows dry and faint. But when we draw near to the Lord in humble trust, He revives our weary hearts with fresh grace.

God also reminds us that He chose us in sovereign love and will never throw us away. We once were captive to sin, but He brought us into His own family. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "our Saviour is no fickle lover." Even though we are as small and needy as insects before His greatness, Christ has already given His life for us, so helping us today is no trouble for Him.

Whenever life brings major changes, new responsibilities, or unfamiliar paths, fear can tempt us to imagine the worst. Yet the Lord reaches out to take hold of our right hand. Bringing our fears straight to Him in prayer breaks the power of panic and restores our confidence in His loving guidance.

questions: What simple habit can you practice today to feed your soul with God's Word and prayer?
What new duty or unknown situation do you need to place into God's guiding hand?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for choosing me in Christ and bringing me into Your family. Forgive me when I try to carry life in my own strength instead of seeking Your renewal. Please take hold of my right hand today, guide my steps, and calm my fears with Your sure help. Amen.

D12.author: Vivian Bricker
D12.work: The Fear of Becoming First-Time Parents
